articles.title: Shreveport man arrested for threatening AG Murrill over prediction markets lawsuit
articles.summary: A Shreveport resident got arrested after threatening Louisiana's Attorney General over his office's lawsuit against prediction market platforms. It's a reminder that the legal war over online betting is heating up enough to make people genuinely unhinged about it.

articles.title: City Council probe finds New Yorkers lost $53M on prediction market platform
articles.summary: A New York City investigation revealed that users lost $53M on a prediction market platform, likely through a combination of poor odds, platform failures, or outright fraud. The probe will probably trigger regulatory scrutiny across the entire prediction market industry and give ammunition to anyone arguing these platforms need stricter guardrails.

articles.title: Utah to Drop Criminal Charges Against Prediction Market Kalshi
articles.summary: Utah's prosecutors are dropping criminal charges against Kalshi, the prediction market platform that's been pushing the boundaries of what you can legally bet on in America. This is a significant win for the industry, signaling that regulators might finally be ready to let prediction markets operate without treating them like the roulette wheel's shady cousin.

articles.title: Simon Denny on Prediction Markets, Speculation, and the Future of Truth
articles.summary: Simon Denny apparently thinks prediction markets are wrestling with deeper questions about how we establish truth in an age of rampant speculation. That matters because if he's right, the legitimacy of prediction markets depends on solving a problem way bigger than getting odds right.

articles.title: KKR Curbs Staff Betting on Prediction Markets
articles.summary: KKR just told its employees to pump the brakes on prediction market gambling, probably because watching your firm's staff gamble on company outcomes looks bad to regulators and LPs. When major finance houses start restricting access, it signals the market's hitting legitimacy thresholds that make the old Wild West rules unworkable.

articles.title: Kalshi daily volume of ‘perps’ trading begins to top its prediction markets
articles.summary: Kalshi's perpetual futures contracts are now generating more daily trading volume than its original prediction market offerings. That's a problem for the prediction market thesis that derivatives exchanges exist primarily to let you bet on binary outcomes.

articles.title: NYC Calls on Kalshi, Polymarket to Testify on Marketing to Youth
articles.summary: NYC regulators are pressuring Kalshi and Polymarket to defend why they're marketing prediction markets to young people, suggesting the city views these platforms as potentially risky gambling products that need age restrictions. If the testimony leads to enforcement action or new regulations, it could crimp user growth for the two biggest US-focused prediction market operators just as the category is hitting mainstream adoption.

articles.title: The line between sports hero and gambling shill is fast disappearing
articles.summary: Athletes are cashing massive checks to promote sportsbooks and betting apps, blurring the line between legitimate sports figures and casino marketing arms. It matters because celebrity endorsements drive retail betting volume, which creates artificial demand spikes that prediction market operators have to hedge against in real time.

articles.title: NFLs WAGs Now Have Prediction Market Sponsorships, Too
articles.summary: The NFL's wives and girlfriends are now cashing in on prediction market sponsorships, turning their social media clout into direct betting platform partnerships. This matters because it signals prediction markets are going mainstream through celebrity endorsements, the same playbook that made daily fantasy sports and sportsbooks household names.

articles.title: Commentary: Rolling the dice on prediction markets: North Carolina's warning for Indiana
articles.summary: North Carolina apparently tried something with prediction markets and it went badly enough to serve as a cautionary tale for Indiana. If states keep banning or botching their regulatory approach, the entire market infrastructure stays fragmented and risky for everyone trying to actually use these things.

articles.title: US Prediction Markets: Modern Timeline
articles.summary: The US finally has a legit timeline for when prediction markets will stop operating in legal gray area and actually become regulated. That matters because right now everyone's guessing what the rules will look like, and the second they're official, the entire market structure probably shifts.

articles.title: $20,000 in Bets, $350,000 in Profit: ‘Suspicious’ Polymarket Clusters Nailed Jensen Huang’s Nvidia Return
articles.summary: Someone made $350K on a $20K bet by timing Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return perfectly on Polymarket, raising fresh questions about whether certain traders have information the rest of us don't. The pattern matters because it's the kind of edge that makes prediction markets either thrillingly efficient or deeply broken depending on who's actually allowed to know what.
